description: Verify that DUT re-picks its Link-Local address after a probing-window conflict ARP Probe (RFC 3927 §2.2.1, MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 3927 §2.2.1 covers the Probe-vs-Probe race: if another host is also probing the same tentative address, both must back off. The conflict signal is an ARP Probe with target_proto_ip = DUT's tentative LL (sender_proto_ip = 0.0.0.0, target_hw = 0). DUT must re-pick.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: OpStartLLAutoconf (kicks the Link-Local state machine)

2. DUT → wire: first ARP Probe with target_proto_ip = tentative_LL

3. Tester → DUT: ARP Probe, sender_proto_ip = 0.0.0.0, target_proto_ip = tentative_LL (a competing prober shape)

4. Observation:
   • DUT → wire: a fresh ARP Probe with target_proto_ip ≠ tentative_LL   ← key check

[Pass condition]
First DUT Probe AND a follow-up Probe targeting a different LL after the competing Probe.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_initial_probe — DUT did not emit any initial ARP Probe within the deadline
• Fail_no_repick — DUT did not re-probe with a different LL after the conflict ARP Probe

verdicts.Pass: DUT re-picked its LL after the conflict ARP Probe — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_initial_probe: DUT did not emit any initial ARP Probe within the deadline
verdicts.Fail_no_repick: DUT did not re-probe with a different LL after the conflict ARP
